faq.mountDevice.q: How do I open a computer's files on my own device?
faq.mountDevice.a: On the Use from your PC tab, choose Open them as a network drive while the computer runs: it shows the address that opens the files as a network drive. On a Mac, choose Go > Connect to Server in Finder and paste the address; Finder opens it read-only. On Windows, open This PC > Map network drive in File Explorer; nothing needs installing, and by default Windows moves files of up to about 50 MB. On Linux, press Ctrl+L in GNOME Files and paste the Linux address; it uses gvfs-backends, which most GNOME desktops have. An iPhone, iPad or Android device needs an app that can open WebDAV drives.
faq.mountLinux.q: How do I mount the files on Linux without a desktop?
faq.mountLinux.a: Install davfs2 once (sudo apt install davfs2, or sudo dnf install davfs2), then run the two lines Mount shows: one makes the folder, one mounts it. The mounted files belong to your user on that machine, with folder and file modes that keep other users of it out. At the user name and password prompts press Enter, unless a password rule protects these files: then give its user name and password. The address is the key: anyone with it can open and change these files.
faq.mountCli.q: Can I mount from the command line or from my code?
faq.mountCli.a: Yes. The Hoody CLI mounts the address on a folder on Mac, Linux and Windows, and can change files. It runs rclone mount, so it needs an rclone that can mount, from rclone.org (Homebrew's rclone can't mount on a Mac), and macFUSE on a Mac, fuse3 on Linux or WinFsp on Windows. Install the CLI with curl -fsSL https://install.hoody.com | sh (macOS, Linux), irm https://install.hoody.com/install.ps1 | iex (Windows) or npm install -g hoody-sdk, or write npx hoody-sdk for hoody. The Hoody SDK does the same from JavaScript or TypeScript. The Use from your PC tab shows the lines for both.
faq.pcNeeds.q: What do I need to use a computer's files from my PC?
faq.pcNeeds.a: The Use from your PC tab shows the lines to run. You need the Hoody CLI (install it, then sign in), rclone v1.61.0 or newer from rclone.org (packages from Linux distributions may be older), and an up-to-date Hoody Kit on the computer. macOS needs macFUSE or FUSE-T. Windows needs WinFsp, and the mount runs in the foreground there. Linux needs fuse3. A mount is not a sync client: a file changed elsewhere at the same time becomes a conflict copy beside it.
faq.pcShare.q: How do I put a folder from my PC into a computer?
faq.pcShare.a: Run the share line on the Use from your PC tab. A folder such as ~/Projects/site then appears on the computer at /hoody/mounts/permanent/site. Add --read-only to share it read-only. While it runs, the folder is a place in Browse, and deleting there deletes the files on your PC. It works only while your PC is online and the command runs; Ctrl+C waits until the computer's writes have reached your PC. See what is shared with hoody share list, and end a share with hoody share stop and its name.
faq.storageConnect.q: Which storage can I connect, and how do I sign in to Google Drive or Dropbox?
faq.storageConnect.a: On the Storage tab, press Add storage, pick the service and fill in its details. The computer checks them with the storage before it keeps them; then you can open it as a folder there. The services include Amazon S3 and S3-compatible ones, SFTP server, WebDAV, MEGA, Windows share (SMB), FTP server, Google Drive, Dropbox, Microsoft OneDrive, pCloud and Box. The sign-in ones take a token you make on your own computer with rclone: the form shows the command, or for OneDrive the steps, and you paste what rclone prints.
faq.storageUploadWait.q: What happens to files I write into a storage folder?
faq.storageUploadWait.a: They are kept on this computer until they reach the storage. Files whose upload stopped wait under Waiting to upload on the Storage tab until you deliver, download or discard them. Deliver sends every complete file to the storage and replaces the copy there, even one changed since; incomplete files stay. Closing a storage folder or removing a storage keeps the files not uploaded yet on this computer.
faq.limits.q: How much can I upload, copy or download at once?
faq.limits.a: One upload takes up to 5,000 files and 50 GB, and up to 10 GB a file. Copy or move to the other side takes up to 100 items a press, with up to 5 of them folders to copy. A download from a link takes up to 100 GiB and 12 hours. A search looks at up to 50,000 items. Folders more than 8 levels deep can't be opened here yet.
